changes.before: Remove L from 1L. What type prints?
changes.after: R distinguishes an integer stored as an integer from an ordinary number written without an integer mark.

before: 1 is normally a double-precision numeric value in R, even though it looks like a whole number.
1L creates an integer value. typeof distinguishes integer from double; both can participate in numeric calculations.
Double precision cannot represent every real number exactly. Integer storage has a finite range; neither type is an unlimited exact arithmetic guarantee.

Complete local R example; the app itself does not execute it:
```r
value <- 1L
cat(typeof(value))
```
Expected output or behavior: integer. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
